resources.string: Nex Macro uses this service to tap and swipe the screen according to the settings you create, and to show its control overlay. No screen data is collected or sent anywhere.

Nex Macro needs the accessibility service to tap and swipe the screen. On the next screen choose \"Nex Macro\" and turn it on.\n\nAndroid 13 and up: if the option is greyed out (app installed outside Play Store), open Nex Macro\'s App Info, tap the ⋮ menu and choose \"Allow restricted settings\".

Run clicks right away when a chosen app opens
Tick the apps that should show the Nex Macro overlay automatically (uses the last mode you used).

Single Target Mode

Please take a moment to read these instructions.

Moving the overlay

Drag the left or right side of the bar to move it anywhere.

Changing the click corner

Tap a side of the bar to change which corner clicks happen at. The active corner is marked by a triangle on the bar and a blue ring on screen. The click lands just outside that corner, so you can click in any corner of the screen.

Starting and stopping

Press ▶: the bar turns green and starts clicking. You cannot move the overlay while running; press ⏸ to pause.

Emergency stop

Locking the phone or turning the screen off stops the app. If the phone freezes, press the power button once.

Closing the overlay

Tap the ✕ symbol to close the overlay and stop the app.

Multi Target Mode

Please take a moment to read these instructions.

Using the overlay

The panel has five buttons whose function differs between tap and hold:

▶ Tap: start / stop clicking.
＋ Tap: add a click target. Hold: add a swipe target.
－ Tap: remove the last target. Hold: remove all targets.
⚙ Tap: open options and configurations.
› Tap: collapse all overlays (a ✕ button appears to close). Hold then drag: reposition the panel.

Adding targets

Each target is numbered and runs in sequence. Clicks/swipes originate from the target's center. After the last target the sequence loops back to the first.

Configuring a target

Tap a target to set its start delay, end delay, duration, repeat, disable-after and randomization radius.

Swipe targets

Holding the ＋ button adds a swipe target: it swipes from the circle labeled "start" to the circle labeled "end".

Proper settings

Your phone and its apps have limits on how fast they can be tapped. Clicking faster than 50 milliseconds may cause an app not to register the click or lock up your phone. If that happens, lock your phone or turn off the screen to stop, then change the configuration.
